summary: This standards-track document carries the image body parts originally defined in RFC 1495, for image formats first defined in MIME, through an X.400 system.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC defines how JPEG and GIF image data can be identified as X.400 body parts and matched to MIME image types. The listed mappings copy the image data without conversion.

questions: how is jpeg carried in x.400
how is jpeg represented in x400
how is gif mapped between x400 and mime
subtitle: X.400 body-part identifiers and MIME mappings for JPEG and GIF images.

tldr.problem: X.400 systems need body parts for image formats defined in MIME.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines JPEG and GIF Extended Body Parts and records their equivalences to MIME types and FTAM body parts.
tldr.outcome: The listed mappings require no content conversion; the RFC says FTAM body-part identifiers may be more useful than the new body parts.

today: RFC 2158 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Images Across Mail Systems
sections.content:
The memo carries body parts defined in RFC 1495 for image formats originally defined in MIME through an X.400 system. It also records object identifiers assigned to these formats as FTAM body parts.

The RFC says the FTAM mappings will probably be more useful than the new body parts it defines.
sections.plainLanguage: The document connects image labels used by MIME with image body parts understood by X.400 and FTAM systems.

sections.title: JPEG and GIF Extended Body Parts
sections.content:
The RFC defines jpeg-body-part and gif-body-part as Extended Body Parts. Neither has parameters; each carries its content as an OCTET STRING whose content is defined by MIME.

The JPEG body part identifier is { mixer-bp-data 3 }, and the GIF identifier is { mixer-bp-data 4 }.
sections.plainLanguage: JPEG and GIF each get a separate X.400 identifier. The image content remains an octet string.

sections.title: MIME and FTAM Equivalences
sections.content:
The RFC maps image/jpeg to the JPEG Extended Body Part and the FTAM EMA JPEG body part. It maps image/gif to the GIF Extended Body Part and the FTAM EMA GIF body part.

All four listed conversions are marked as none. The RFC says security issues are not considered in this memo.
sections.plainLanguage: The mapping table pairs each MIME image type with X.400 and FTAM forms. It specifies no conversion of the image data.

references.text: Freed, N., and N. Borenstein, "Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (MIME) Part One: Format of Internet Message Bodies", RFC 2045, November 1996.
